head: Metal
Observations
rows: floats, fizzes steadily, slowly gets smaller
floats, melts into a ball, whizzes around, fizzes
floats, whizzes, burns with a lilac flame, may crackle

questions.q: Write the word equation for potassium and water.
questions.model: Metal + water gives metal hydroxide + hydrogen. So: potassium + water → potassium hydroxide + hydrogen.

questions.q: Why does sodium melt into a ball?
questions.a: The reaction gives out heat and sodium has a low melting point

questions.q: From the demonstration, write observations and a word equation for each metal, then describe the reactivity trend.
questions.a: As in the table; reactivity increases Li < Na < K
questions.model: Teacher writes the lithium row on screen.

questions.q: Predict what rubidium would do in water.
questions.a: React even more violently, possibly explosively, making rubidium hydroxide and hydrogen.

questions.q: Why are only tiny pieces used, behind a screen?
questions.a: The reactions give out heat and flammable hydrogen; bigger pieces can explode and spit alkali.

Big question: why are they stored under oil?
questions.a: Oil keeps out air and water, which they react with.
